Where it began

Ravindra Jadeja comes from Navagam Ghed, in the Jamnagar district of Gujarat, where he was born on 6 December 1988. He first played for India's under-19 side in 2005, at sixteen, and three years later he was vice-captain of the team that won the 2008 Under-19 World Cup, taking 10 wickets at 13.60.

For Saurashtra he became a run machine. He made three first-class triple hundreds by the age of 23, the first Indian to do it and only the eighth player anywhere, in a list that includes Bradman and Lara.

The player

He first played Test cricket at Nagpur, against England, in December 2012. A few months later he took 24 wickets as India beat Australia 4-0 at home, getting the better of the Australian captain Michael Clarke five times out of six. When Australia came back in 2017 he took 25 wickets and was player of the series, and he and Ravichandran Ashwin became the first spin pair to share the top spot in the Test bowling rankings.

By October 2026 he had played 91 Tests, with 356 wickets at 25.30, including 15 five-wicket innings and a best of 7 for 42, and 4,160 runs at 37.82 with six hundreds and 28 fifties. His 175 not out against Sri Lanka in 2022 is the highest Test score by an Indian batting at seven or lower. He ranks 26th among all Test wicket-takers, and in 2021 he was the world's top-ranked Test all-rounder.

What made him special

With the ball he is accurate and hard to get away, and he has been ranked the best bowler in the world. In the field he is among the finest of his generation, and his run outs have ended many a promising partnership.

In his first big home series the bat was mostly along for the ride. It has since made up for lost time, and then some.

Away from the middle

Shane Warne, his first IPL captain at Rajasthan Royals, called him Rockstar, and the name stuck. MS Dhoni calls him Jaddu, the name on his IPL shirt. Fans online took to calling him Sir Jadeja as a running joke, and he said he was quite happy with the title. He received the Arjuna Award in 2019.

He has a habit of being there at the finish. He hit a six and a four off the last two balls to win the 2023 IPL final for Chennai Super Kings, and he struck the winning boundary in the 2025 Champions Trophy final.

And finally

Few cricketers have been so useful in so many places at once. Captains have been known to give him the ball, put him in the field where the catches go and send him in at seven, and then wonder what they were worrying about.
